speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy experiencing feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. To help me understand what is wrong, can you tell me if these symptoms have been getting worse over the past few weeks?

Also, have you noticed any vomiting, especially if it looks like it contains bile (green) or if you see white, chalky material in your stools?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The baby seems to be in significant pain with abdominal tenderness and reduced oral intake. Are the stools currently loose or watery, and have you noticed any signs of dehydration such as fewer wet diapers or a sunken soft spot?

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dilated bowel segments with absence of gas in the rectum, suggesting a possible obstruction

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Patient
text: The abdomen still looks swollen and the baby seems uncomfortable, especially in the lower abdomen. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Intussusception and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Intussusception. The clinical presentation of an 8-month-old with intermittent abdominal pain (crying on palpation), abdominal distension, and a previous medical opinion strongly supports this diagnosis. Please ensure an ultrasound is performed immediately to confirm the diagnosis and facilitate potential reduction.
